open_points.subject: A13 owner-session identity
open_points.text: The session's identity ... [is] at least 32 bytes from the operating system's random source
open_points.question: What must Registry do if a newly generated owner-session identity equals an identity of an existing live session?
options: Generate again until the identity is unused
Replace or reuse the existing session
Fail the sign-in
open_points.default_guess: Generate again until the identity is unused.

open_points.subject: A13 concurrent sign-ins
open_points.text: Concurrent sign-ins are counted one at a time.
open_points.question: In what order are concurrent sign-ins applied when their order changes the result, such as a correct credential racing the fifth refused credential?
options: Order by request arrival
Either serial order is permitted
Give a successful credential precedence
Give the refusal that starts lockout precedence

open_points.subject: A13 concurrent owner-session requests
open_points.text: The requests of one owner session that change its state ... are applied one at a time: each sees the session as the one before left it
open_points.question: Which serial order applies to concurrent uploads, confirmation displays, submissions and sign-out requests when different orders produce different accepted actions?
options: Order by request arrival
Either serial order is permitted
Use a fixed precedence by request kind

open_points.subject: A13 confirmation validation
open_points.text: A submission carries it when it passes the owner session and CSRF checks ... and gives a value equal to the pending one; from there on, whatever the answer — a binding to another action or input included — the pending value is used up.
open_points.question: At which check are the confirmation's action, target, revision or access version, input digest and age validated, and which failure wins when more than one of them is wrong?
options: Validate all confirmation properties in A04 stage 1
Validate only session, CSRF, value and age in stage 1, then binding data in stages 3–5
Report every failed confirmation property together
open_points.default_guess: Validate the session, CSRF, confirmation value and age in stage 1, consume the matching value, then apply target, input and version checks in their A04 stages.

open_points.subject: A16 picked records and foreign project references
open_points.text: a room or pointer naming another project belongs to that project: records only of projects the owner did not pick are neither checked ...; A picked project whose room names a project absent from the file refuses the import as malformed.
open_points.question: If a room or pointer is structurally contained under a picked project but names a different or absent project, is it ignored as belonging to an unpicked project or does it make the picked project malformed?
options: Refuse the import as malformed
Ignore the record unless the project it names is picked
Treat structural containment as authoritative and import it with the picked project

open_points.subject: A16 references to rooms
open_points.text: A brought-in record is malformed when ... it names a project or room the file does not hold
open_points.question: Which imported record kinds are allowed to name a room, given that State 1's imported Project, Room and ArtifactPointer facts define no room reference except a Room's own identity?
options: No record names a room, so this condition is inapplicable
The migration format adds a room reference to pointers
Another migration-only record may name a room
open_points.default_guess: No imported record names a room; remove or declare this condition inapplicable.

open_points.subject: A16 imported vocabularies
open_points.text: A brought-in record is malformed when ... a status is outside its vocabulary ...; For each Customer it will make, the owner gives its name and kind
open_points.question: Must confirmation refuse an invalid object kind, customer kind or other non-status closed-vocabulary value, and at which step is that reported?
options: Refuse every value outside any declared vocabulary at mapping and confirmation
Validate only statuses and pointer types during import
Leave non-status vocabulary validation to the later file contract
open_points.default_guess: Refuse every value outside its declared vocabulary, show it in the mapping, and recheck it at confirmation.

open_points.subject: A16 replacement by an identical upload
open_points.text: another file is uploaded in that session [so the old file is dropped] ... the confirmation applies the file of that digest ... Confirming a mapping after another file was uploaded in the session is refused
open_points.question: Does uploading byte-for-byte identical content with the same digest invalidate a pending confirmation for the previous upload?
options: Yes, every accepted upload replaces the upload instance and invalidates its confirmation
No, the same digest means the confirmed file is still kept
Only a different digest invalidates it
open_points.default_guess: Yes, every accepted upload is a replacement and requires a newly shown confirmation.

open_points.subject: A16 post-import backup
open_points.text: right after it ... Registry makes a backup run outside the daily schedule ... a failed run is retried at the next run
open_points.question: If Registry stops or crashes after the import transaction commits but before the post-import backup run starts or records an outcome, how does the next start know that the extra post-import backup is still due?
options: The migration closure persistently implies the run is due until a checked backup names that import
The extra run is lost and only the next ordinary daily backup is made
Persist a separate post-import-backup-pending fact
open_points.default_guess: Treat the closure as requiring a checked post-import backup until a kept backup can be shown to contain it.

open_points.subject: A17 owner-only token configuration
open_points.text: one service token for each service ... or, for an owner-only start, none of the four; ... A missing, malformed or unknown item fails the start; Registry applies no default to any item.
open_points.question: How is an intentional owner-only start distinguished from an accidentally missing set of all four token items, and are absent, null and blank token entries equivalent?
options: All four token keys absent means owner-only; null or blank is malformed
An explicit owner-only configuration flag is required
All four absent, null or blank mean owner-only
open_points.default_guess: All four token keys absent means owner-only; any present blank or malformed token fails.

open_points.subject: A17 startup check order
open_points.text: The checks run in the order of these rules and the first that fails stops the start
open_points.question: What is the order among multiple items checked inside the same rule, such as the four token lengths, pairwise secret equality checks, unknown items and multiple path failures?
options: Declare a fixed item-by-item order
Report all failures within the first failing rule
Any order within a rule is permitted
open_points.default_guess: Use a declared fixed order matching the configuration item list and stop at its first failure.

open_points.subject: A17 secret representation
open_points.text: A secret ... is at least 32 bytes long; ... No two secrets are equal
open_points.question: Which byte representation is used for length, equality and constant-time comparison when configuration supplies textual credentials or an encoded backup key?
options: Compare the exact encoded bytes presented by configuration
Decode each secret using a declared encoding and compare decoded bytes
Count Unicode characters for textual credentials
open_points.default_guess: Require a declared ASCII-safe encoding and compare its decoded secret bytes.

open_points.subject: A18 backup cryptography
open_points.text: Each backup is encrypted with the backup key ... A backup records ... a digest of the key ... A backup cannot be read without the key
open_points.question: Which authenticated-encryption algorithm, nonce generation, key interpretation or derivation, metadata authentication and key-digest algorithm make these guarantees verifiable?
options: Declare one authenticated-encryption format and digest algorithm
Leave the cryptographic construction to the implementation
Use the store engine's encryption format
open_points.default_guess: Declare a versioned authenticated-encryption format using a random nonce and authenticate all readable metadata, with a separately declared cryptographic key fingerprint.

open_points.subject: A18 backup-file recognition
open_points.text: the kept backups themselves saying which days have one ... a status file ... is rewritten at start from the kept backups
open_points.question: What happens when a file under the kept-backup prefix has unreadable, malformed or unauthenticated metadata: does it count as a kept backup, block a run, get deleted, or get ignored?
options: Treat it as a failed backup, report it and delete it
Ignore it and leave it untouched
Fail status reconstruction and skip the new backup
Stop Registry from serving
open_points.default_guess: Report it as a failed backup, delete it if possible, and do not count it for scheduling or status.

open_points.subject: A18 simultaneous backup runs
open_points.text: a run that falls due while another runs waits for it, and both are made
open_points.question: When the ordinary daily run and the post-import run become due concurrently, which runs first and which store snapshot is each required to contain?
options: Post-import run first, then ordinary run
Ordinary run first, then post-import run
Either serial order is permitted, with each copying the store at its own start
open_points.default_guess: Post-import run first, then the ordinary run, with each copying the store at its own start.

open_points.subject: A18 retention deletion failures
open_points.text: Registry deletes every backup made more than 30 × 24 hours before ... a deletion that fails ... is tried again at the next run ... Every phase runs even when an earlier one failed
open_points.question: If deleting one expired backup fails, does Registry continue attempting the other expired backups during that run, and how are multiple failures represented in the outcome?
options: Continue every deletion and report all failures
Stop the deletion phase at the first failure
Retry the failed deletion immediately before continuing
open_points.default_guess: Continue attempting every expired backup and report every failed deletion.

open_points.subject: A04 confirmation check stage
open_points.text: stage (1) ... a confirmation value where one is asked; ... stage (3) ... target ... stage (4) the values given; stage (5) the stated revision or access version
open_points.question: Does stage 1 check only that a matching, unexpired confirmation value exists, or also its binding to the target, inputs and revision, which A04 otherwise assigns to later stages?
options: Stage 1 checks the entire confirmation binding
Stage 1 checks session, CSRF, value and expiry only; later stages check the bound target, inputs and version
Each property is checked twice
open_points.default_guess: Stage 1 checks session, CSRF, confirmation value and expiry only; the binding is compared when the corresponding later-stage value is checked.

open_points.subject: A04 malformed identities versus existence
open_points.text: (3) that every record the action names exists ...; (4) the values given
open_points.question: When a supplied identity cannot be parsed or violates its value format, is it refused as an invalid value at stage 4 or treated as a non-existent record at stage 3, which is ordered first?
options: Parse enough to identify valid identities before stage 3 and report malformed identities as stage-4 value failures
Treat every malformed identity as not found at stage 3
Add identity syntax validation before the existence stage
open_points.default_guess: Add identity syntax validation before existence; only syntactically valid identities proceed to the stage-3 lookup.

open_points.subject: M11 uploaded import file
open_points.text: at most one uploaded import file ... Everything in it ends with the session ... Temporary runtime state; never a durable record beyond its life
open_points.question: May the uploaded personal-data file be spooled to disk, and what cleanup guarantee applies on replacement, acceptance, sign-out, expiry, restart or process failure so that it does not survive its owner session?
options: Keep it only in memory
Allow a dedicated temporary file that is synchronously removed on normal endings and swept at every start
Allow ordinary framework temporary storage with implementation-defined cleanup
open_points.default_guess: Allow only a dedicated temporary file outside the store, remove it on every normal ending or replacement, and sweep all such files at startup after a crash.
